title: Paced outbound calls to a courier quote API
name: Courier quote pacer

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code limits the rate of calls to the courier API? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Ten quote requests arrive at once on an idle service. Roughly when does the tenth courier API call start?
choices: After about 2 seconds, once the first call's timeout expires

questions.prompt: The courier API slows down so each call takes 1.5 seconds. What happens to concurrency?
choices: Calls still start every 200 ms, so up to about 8 can be in flight at once
Only one call is in flight at a time because the executor waits for each task
The executor stops starting calls until the slow ones finish

questions.prompt: During a spike, 80 quote requests arrive within a few milliseconds. What do callers see?
choices: All 80 get real quotes, just later
The first 50 are queued; the rest throw QueueFullError to the caller of quote()
Roughly the first 50 queue for real quotes; the remaining ~30 immediately get the fallback quote marked estimated
